def _exposed_result_ids(
    results: Sequence[ResultRead], *, expectation_types: Mapping[uuid.UUID, str]
) -> list[str]:
    """Which of these results actually surfaced regulated data to the caller.

    `redaction` is the state the redactor computed for THIS read: `full` means
    everything row-level was masked, `null` means the result carried no row-level
    content at all. Neither exposed anything, so neither belongs in the list an
    investigator reads to answer "who saw the failing rows?".

    `observed_value` is the OTHER door to raw cells and needs its own test, not a
    null check — see `observed_value_exposes_cells`. The first version here asked
    only whether it was non-None, which marked a fully-masked list and a plain row
    count alike as exposures, so effectively every read was recorded as one.
    `expectation_types` (`check_id` → `expectation_type`, #1486) is what lets that
    test tell a max/min's literal cell apart from an aggregate statistic that also
    happens to have a tested column — a missing entry (a deleted check) falls back
    to "not a known cell-reporting type", same as before #1486.

    Derived from the redacted output rather than from the stored row, deliberately
    — the same column policy that decides what the caller sees decides what the
    audit records, so the two can never disagree about whether an exposure
    happened.
    """
    return [
        str(r.id)
        for r in results
        if r.redaction in {"none", "partial"}
        or svc.observed_value_exposes_cells(
            r.observed_value, expectation_type=expectation_types.get(r.check_id)
        )
    ]


def _audit_result_read(
    db: Session,
    user: User,
    *,
    run: Any,
    results: Sequence[ResultRead],
    expectation_types: Mapping[uuid.UUID, str],
) -> None:
    """Record a read of a run's results (G1 / #431, `action_class='access'`).

    ONE event per read, not per result: the act is "this person opened this run",
    and N events for one page would bury the acts an investigator is looking for
    under the mechanics of how the page is assembled. The individual result ids
    are in the payload, so nothing is lost.

    Records WHICH results exposed regulated data, never WHAT they contained (ADR
    0041 §2.6.3) — copying samples into an append-only table with a longer
    retention would defeat the #1253 purge and the #432 erasure path.
    """
    exposed = _exposed_result_ids(results, expectation_types=expectation_types)
    audit_service.record_access(
        db,
        action="run_results.read",
        entity_type="run",
        entity_id=run.id,
        actor=user,
        exposed=bool(exposed),
        detail={
            "suite_id": str(run.suite_id),
            "result_count": len(results),
            "exposed_result_ids": exposed,
        },
    )

@router.get("/runs/{run_id}", response_model=RunDetailRead, summary="Get a run with its results")
def get_run(
    run_id: uuid.UUID,
    current_user: Annotated[User, Depends(get_current_user)],
    db: Annotated[Session, Depends(get_db)],
) -> RunDetailRead:
    run = svc.get_run(db, run_id)
    if run is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="run not found")
    # Gate on the run's suite: a caller who can't see the suite can't see its
    # runs (404 hides the run id too, matching the suite existence-hiding rule).
    suite = require_permission(db, run.suite_id, current_user.id, minimum="view")
    results = svc.list_results(db, run_id)
    # Map check_id → tested column so each result's sample is redacted column-aware
    # against the suite's policy (#415): a non-PII tested column's values surface.
    checks = {c.id: c for c in db.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == run.suite_id))}
    policy = suite.column_policy
    tags = _asset_column_tags(db, suite, run)
    # `Run` has no `results` relationship to validate a RunDetailRead from
    # directly, so validate the run fields (as RunRead), graft the data-quality
    # outcome (#571 — else checks_total/passed stay at the 0/0 default here), and
    # attach the separately-fetched, redaction-gated results.
    outcome = svc.check_outcome_counts(db, [run.id]).get(run.id)
    reads = [
        _result_read(
            r,
            tested_column=(
                checks[r.check_id].config.get("column") if r.check_id in checks else None
            ),
            policy=policy,
            tags=tags,
        )
        for r in results
    ]
    expectation_types = {check_id: check.expectation_type for check_id, check in checks.items()}
    _audit_result_read(
        db, current_user, run=run, results=reads, expectation_types=expectation_types
    )

unresolvable target (orchestration connection, garbage config) returns None
without raising. Skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL.

    db_session.add(u)
    db_session.flush()
    return u


def _connection(
    db_session: Any,
    *,
    type_: str = "snowflake",
    env: str = "dev",

) -> Connection:
    conn = Connection(

"""`run_service.historical_check_context` — #1489.

Redaction (`tested_column`) and the G1 access-exposure audit (`expectation_type`,
#1486) both need to know what a check WAS measuring when a given result was
written, not what it measures NOW — `expectation_type`/`config` are freely
PATCH-able on a live `Check` with no re-validation against existing results.
Verifies the resolution picks the `check_versions` snapshot in effect at each
result's own `created_at`, and falls back sanely when there is no history.

Skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

from backend.app.db.models import Check, CheckVersion, Connection, Result, Run, Suite, User
from backend.app.services import run_service

_T0 = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)


def _suite_and_check(
    db_session: Any, *, expectation_type: str = "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null"
) -> tuple[Suite, Check]:
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"o-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="snowflake",
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "x"},
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.flush()
    suite = Suite(name="orders", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id)
    db_session.add(suite)
    db_session.flush()
    check = Check(
        suite_id=suite.id,
        name="values",
        kind="expectation",
        expectation_type=expectation_type,
        config={"column": "LIVE_COLUMN"},
    )
    db_session.add(check)
    db_session.flush()
    return suite, check


def _version(
    db_session: Any,
    check: Check,
    *,
    version_no: int,
    created_at: datetime,
    expectation_type: str,
    column: str,
) -> CheckVersion:
    version = CheckVersion(
        check_id=check.id,
        version_no=version_no,
        name=check.name,
        kind=check.kind,
        expectation_type=expectation_type,
        config={"column": column},
        created_at=created_at,
    )
    db_session.add(version)
    db_session.flush()
    return version


def _result(db_session: Any, check: Check, *, created_at: datetime) -> Result:
    run = Run(suite_id=check.suite_id, status="succeeded", triggered_by="manual")
    db_session.add(run)
    db_session.flush()
    result = Result(run_id=run.id, check_id=check.id, status="fail", created_at=created_at)
    db_session.add(result)
    db_session.flush()
    return result


def test_resolves_the_version_in_effect_when_each_result_was_written(db_session: Any) -> None:
    # #1486's own motivating case: a check that reported a MEAN when a result
    # was written, later edited to MAX/MIN — the old result must not retroactively
    # look like a literal-cell exposure. The live Check row is deliberately a
    # THIRD value neither version used, so a fallback-to-live bug can't hide
    # behind an accidental match.
    _suite, check = _suite_and_check(db_session, expectation_type="expect_table_row_count_to_equal")
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=1,
        created_at=_T0,
        expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
        column="v1_column",
    )
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=2,
        created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=1),
        expectation_type="expect_column_max_to_be_between",
        column="v2_column",
    )
    before_edit = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0 + timedelta(hours=1))
    after_edit = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=2))

    context = run_service.historical_check_context(
        db_session, [before_edit, after_edit], {check.id: check}
    )

    assert context[before_edit.id] == ("v1_column", "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null")

def _suite_and_check(
    db_session: Any, *, expectation_type: str = "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null"
) -> tuple[Suite, Check]:
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"o-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()

def create_check(
    session: Session,
    *,
    suite_id: uuid.UUID,
    name: str,
    kind: str,
    expectation_type: str,
    config: dict[str, Any],
    warn_threshold: Decimal | None,
    fail_threshold: Decimal | None,
    critical_threshold: Decimal | None,
    source_connection_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
    dimension: str | None = None,
    actor_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
) -> Check:
    """Create a check in a suite, recording its first version (#280).

    `dimension` (ADR 0038) is the author's optional override; omitted, it is
    DERIVED from the expectation type/kind. Note that omitting it does not mean
    "unclassified" — only a check whose type has no derivation lands NULL.

    Raises `SuiteNotFoundError` (404) if the suite does not exist, or
    `CheckConfigInvalidError` (422) for an unsupported kind.
    """
    suite = get_suite(session, suite_id)  # 404 if the suite is missing
    validate_kind(kind)
    validate_lengths(name=name, expectation_type=expectation_type)
    validate_threshold_ordering(
        warn_threshold=warn_threshold,
        fail_threshold=fail_threshold,
        critical_threshold=critical_threshold,
    )

def test_the_access_commit_does_not_expire_the_callers_objects(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any
) -> None:
    """`expire_on_commit` is True by default, and a read path commits in the
    MIDDLE of building its response.

    Left unsuppressed, every ORM object the caller still holds is expired, so a
    50-result run issues ~50 refresh SELECTs on the attribute access that follows
    — and a row deleted concurrently raises `ObjectDeletedError`, a 500 caused
    entirely by the audit write, on the path whose own AC forbids a latency
    regression.

    Asserted through the response rather than by counting queries: if the objects
    had been expired and the row was gone, the request would not have returned
    its data at all.
    """
    _owner, run = _seed(
        db_session,
        sample={"partial_unexpected_list": [1], "unexpected_count": 1},
        column="line_total",
    )
    resp = client.get(f"/api/v1/runs/{run.id}")
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json()["results"], "the response must survive the access commit"

    # every later commit in the process silently stops expiring.
    assert db_session.expire_on_commit is True

def test_editing_a_check_does_not_retroactively_relabel_an_old_result(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any
) -> None:
    """A result must be classified by what the check WAS when the row was
    written, not what it is now.

    Real end-to-end repro of the #1489 gap: a check is created reporting a MEAN
    (never a cell), a result is written under that version, and the check is
    THEN edited via the real `check_service.update_check` path to a MAX/MIN type
    on a different (PII) column — the exact edit `update_check` allows with no
    re-validation against existing results. Re-reading the OLD result must still
    see it as the harmless mean it always was: neither a newly-invented cell
    exposure in the audit, nor a newly-applied mask on a column it was never

"""`run_service.historical_check_context` — #1489.

Redaction (`tested_column`) and the G1 access-exposure audit (`expectation_type`,
#1486) both need to know what a check WAS measuring when a given result was
written, not what it measures NOW — `expectation_type`/`config` are freely
PATCH-able on a live `Check` with no re-validation against existing results.
Verifies the resolution picks the `check_versions` snapshot in effect at each
result's own `created_at`, and falls back sanely when there is no history.

Skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

from backend.app.db.models import Check, CheckVersion, Connection, Result, Run, Suite, User
from backend.app.services import run_service

_T0 = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)


def _suite_and_check(
    db_session: Any, *, expectation_type: str = "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null"
) -> tuple[Suite, Check]:
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"o-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="snowflake",
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "x"},
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.flush()
    suite = Suite(name="orders", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id)
    db_session.add(suite)
    db_session.flush()
    check = Check(
        suite_id=suite.id,
        name="values",
        kind="expectation",
        expectation_type=expectation_type,
        config={"column": "LIVE_COLUMN"},
    )
    db_session.add(check)
    db_session.flush()
    return suite, check


def _version(
    db_session: Any,
    check: Check,
    *,
    version_no: int,
    created_at: datetime,
    expectation_type: str,
    column: str,
) -> CheckVersion:
    version = CheckVersion(
        check_id=check.id,
        version_no=version_no,
        name=check.name,
        kind=check.kind,
        expectation_type=expectation_type,
        config={"column": column},
        created_at=created_at,
    )
    db_session.add(version)
    db_session.flush()
    return version


def _result(db_session: Any, check: Check, *, created_at: datetime) -> Result:
    run = Run(suite_id=check.suite_id, status="succeeded", triggered_by="manual")
    db_session.add(run)
    db_session.flush()
    result = Result(run_id=run.id, check_id=check.id, status="fail", created_at=created_at)
    db_session.add(result)
    db_session.flush()
    return result


def test_resolves_the_version_in_effect_when_each_result_was_written(db_session: Any) -> None:
    # #1486's own motivating case: a check that reported a MEAN when a result
    # was written, later edited to MAX/MIN — the old result must not retroactively
    # look like a literal-cell exposure. The live Check row is deliberately a
    # THIRD value neither version used, so a fallback-to-live bug can't hide
    # behind an accidental match.
    _suite, check = _suite_and_check(db_session, expectation_type="expect_table_row_count_to_equal")
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=1,
        created_at=_T0,
        expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
        column="v1_column",
    )
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=2,
        created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=1),
        expectation_type="expect_column_max_to_be_between",
        column="v2_column",
    )
    before_edit = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0 + timedelta(hours=1))
    after_edit = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=2))

    context = run_service.historical_check_context(
        db_session, [before_edit, after_edit], {check.id: check}
    )

    assert context[before_edit.id] == ("v1_column", "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null")
    assert context[after_edit.id] == ("v2_column", "expect_column_max_to_be_between")


def test_falls_back_to_the_live_check_with_no_version_history(db_session: Any) -> None:
    # A check created before #280 shipped (or seeded directly, bypassing
    # check_service) has no check_versions rows at all — no worse off than
    # before this function existed.
    _suite, check = _suite_and_check(db_session, expectation_type="expect_column_max_to_be_between")
    result = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0)

    context = run_service.historical_check_context(db_session, [result], {check.id: check})

    assert context[result.id] == ("LIVE_COLUMN", "expect_column_max_to_be_between")


def test_falls_back_to_the_earliest_version_when_the_result_predates_it(db_session: Any) -> None:
    # Clock skew / same-instant edge case: every version is AFTER the result's
    # created_at. "Before the first edit" is a closer approximation of history
    # than jumping to whatever the check is today.
    _suite, check = _suite_and_check(db_session)
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=1,
        created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=1),
        expectation_type="expect_column_min_to_be_between",
        column="earliest_column",
    )
    result = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0)

    context = run_service.historical_check_context(db_session, [result], {check.id: check})

    assert context[result.id] == ("earliest_column", "expect_column_min_to_be_between")


def test_a_result_with_no_check_id_resolves_to_none() -> None:
    # Defensive: a result whose check was hard-deleted (nullable FK path, if it
    # ever exists) must not raise.
    result = Result(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        run_id=uuid.uuid4(),
        check_id=None,  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        status="fail",
        created_at=_T0,
    )
    context = run_service.historical_check_context(None, [result], {})  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    assert context[result.id] == (None, None)

input.prompt:
We just fixed issue #1489 in the DataQ repo. Background: `run_service.observed_value_exposes_cells` and `redact_observed_value`/`redact_sample_failures` classify a `Result` row using the CHECK's `expectation_type`/`config["column"]`, but those callers used to read them straight off the LIVE `Check` row — which is freely editable via `check_service.update_check` with no re-validation against existing results. So editing a check after results exist could retroactively relabel old results (e.g. a genuine mean gets misclassified as an exposed max/min cell once the check is later edited to a max/min type).

The fix added a new function `historical_check_context(session, results, checks)` in `backend/app/services/run_service.py` (search for `def historical_check_context`). It resolves, per Result, the `(tested_column, expectation_type)` that was actually in effect at `result.created_at`, by looking at `check_versions` rows (an immutable snapshot table already written on every check create/update, unrelated to this PR) and picking the most recent version at-or-before the result's timestamp; falls back to the live `Check` row if the check has no version history at all.

Two call sites were updated to use this instead of reading the live `Check` row directly: `backend/app/api/v1/runs.py`'s `get_run` function (look for the line `context = svc.historical_check_context(db, results, checks)`), and `backend/app/mcp/server.py`'s `_run_results_payload` function (look for `context = run_service.historical_check_context(session, results, checks)`).

New regression tests to verify:

1. `backend/tests/services/test_historical_check_context.py` (a new file) — unit-level tests directly against `historical_check_context`, using a real Postgres test DB (`db_session` fixture). The key one: `test_resolves_the_version_in_effect_when_each_result_was_written` — creates two `CheckVersion` rows with different `(created_at, expectation_type, config)` and two `Result` rows with `created_at` timestamps that fall before/after the edit, and asserts each result resolves to the RIGHT version's data (not the live Check row, which is deliberately given a THIRD, different expectation_type so a "just returns live check" bug can't accidentally match).

2. `backend/tests/api/test_access_events.py` — a new end-to-end test `test_editing_a_check_does_not_retroactively_relabel_an_old_result`: creates a check via the REAL `check_service.create_check` reporting `expect_column_mean_to_be_between` on `line_total`, writes a `Result` with `observed_value={"observed_value": 1250.5}`, then edits the check via the REAL `check_service.update_check` to `expect_column_max_to_be_between` on a different (PII-named) column `customer_email`. Then does `client.get(f"/api/v1/runs/{run.id}")` and asserts the G1 audit event's `exposed` field is `False` — i.e. the old mean-result must NOT be retroactively counted as an exposed cell just because the check was later edited to a cell-reporting type.

def test_editing_a_check_does_not_retroactively_relabel_an_old_result(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any
) -> None:
    """A result must be classified by what the check WAS when the row was
    written, not what it is now.

    Real end-to-end repro of the #1489 gap: a check is created reporting a MEAN
    (never a cell), a result is written under that version, and the check is
    THEN edited via the real `check_service.update_check` path to a MAX/MIN type
    on a different (PII) column — the exact edit `update_check` allows with no
    re-validation against existing results. Re-reading the OLD result must still
    see it as the harmless mean it always was: neither a newly-invented cell
    exposure in the audit, nor a newly-applied mask on a column it was never
    actually redacted against.
    """
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"o-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="snowflake",
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "x"},
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.flush()
    suite = Suite(name="orders", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id)
    db_session.add(suite)
    db_session.commit()

    check = check_service.create_check(
        db_session,
        suite_id=suite.id,
        name="avg",
        kind="expectation",
        expectation_type="expect_column_mean_to_be_between",
        config={"column": "line_total"},
        warn_threshold=None,
        fail_threshold=None,
        critical_threshold=None,
    )
    run = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status="succeeded", triggered_by="manual")
    db_session.add(run)
    db_session.flush()
    db_session.add(
        Result(
            run_id=run.id,
            check_id=check.id,
            status="pass",
            observed_value={"observed_value": 1250.5},
        )
    )
    db_session.commit()

    # The edit #1489 is about: expectation_type AND the tested column both
    # change, onto a PII-named column a max/min check would genuinely expose.
    check_service.update_check(
        db_session,
        suite.id,
        check.id,
        expectation_type="expect_column_max_to_be_between",
        config={"column": "customer_email"},
    )
    db_session.commit()

    app.dependency_overrides[get_current_user] = lambda: owner
    resp = client.get(f"/api/v1/runs/{run.id}")
    assert resp.status_code == 200, resp.text

    event = _events(db_session, "run_results.read", run.id)[0]
    assert event.after is not None
    assert event.after["exposed"] is False, (
        "the mean was never a cell — re-reading it after the check was edited to "
        "a max/min type must not retroactively count it as one"
    )

def test_editing_a_check_does_not_retroactively_relabel_an_old_result(
    client: TestClient, db_session: Any
) -> None:
    """A result must be classified by what the check WAS when the row was
    written, not what it is now.

    Real end-to-end repro of the #1489 gap: a check is created reporting a MEAN
    (never a cell), a result is written under that version, and the check is
    THEN edited via the real `check_service.update_check` path to a MAX/MIN
    type on a different, deliberately NON-PII column — the exact edit
    `update_check` allows with no re-validation against existing results.
    Re-reading the OLD result must still see it as the harmless mean it always
    was, not a newly-invented cell exposure.

    The post-edit column is deliberately non-PII (`unit_price`, not e.g.
    `customer_email`): a PII-named column masks regardless of expectation type,
    which would make `exposed is False` true for the WRONG reason under the
    unfixed code too (masked because the name looks sensitive, not because the
    resolution is historically correct) — a vacuous version of this test caught
    by mutation-checking it. With a non-PII column, the unfixed code shows the
    raw scalar as a genuine max/min cell (`exposed=True`, wrong); only the fix
    correctly attributes the old result to its pre-edit mean version.
    """
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"o-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="snowflake",
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "x"},
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.flush()
    suite = Suite(name="orders", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id)
    db_session.add(suite)
    db_session.commit()

    check = check_service.create_check(
        db_session,
        suite_id=suite.id,
        name="avg",
        kind="expectation",
        expectation_type="expect_column_mean_to_be_between",
        config={"column": "line_total"},
        warn_threshold=None,
        fail_threshold=None,
        critical_threshold=None,
    )
    run = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status="succeeded", triggered_by="manual")
    db_session.add(run)
    db_session.flush()
    db_session.add(
        Result(
            run_id=run.id,
            check_id=check.id,
            status="pass",
            observed_value={"observed_value": 1250.5},
        )
    )
    db_session.commit()

    # The edit #1489 is about: expectation_type AND the tested column both
    # change. Non-PII column (see the docstring above for why that matters).
    check_service.update_check(
        db_session,
        suite.id,
        check.id,
        expectation_type="expect_column_max_to_be_between",
        config={"column": "unit_price"},
    )
    db_session.commit()

    app.dependency_overrides[get_current_user] = lambda: owner
    resp = client.get(f"/api/v1/runs/{run.id}")
    assert resp.status_code == 200, resp.text

    import sys

    from backend.app.db.models import CheckVersion

    result_row = db_session.scalars(select(Result).where(Result.check_id == check.id)).one()
    for v in db_session.scalars(
        select(CheckVersion)
        .where(CheckVersion.check_id == check.id)
        .order_by(CheckVersion.created_at)
    ):
        print("VERSION", v.version_no, v.created_at, v.expectation_type, v.config, file=sys.stderr)
    print("RESULT", result_row.created_at, file=sys.stderr)

    event = _events(db_session, "run_results.read", run.id)[0]
    assert event.after is not None
    assert event.after["exposed"] is False, (
        "the mean was never a cell — re-reading it after the check was edited to "
        "a max/min type must not retroactively count it as one"
    )

title:	fix: redaction and G1 audit resolve check context as of the result's own timestamp (#1489)
state:	OPEN
author:	TheurgicDuke771 (Arijit Roy)
labels:	
assignees:	
reviewers:	
projects:	
milestone:	v1.1 Backlog
number:	1490
url:	https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1490
additions:	530
deletions:	34
auto-merge:	disabled
--
## Summary

- `redact_observed_value`/`redact_sample_failures` (`tested_column`) and `observed_value_exposes_cells` (`expectation_type`, #1486) classify a `Result` row using the CHECK's **current** `expectation_type`/`config["column"]`. Both are freely PATCH-able via `check_service.update_check` with no re-validation against existing results, so editing a check after results exist silently re-labels history — a genuine mean result gets misclassified as an exposed max/min cell once the check is later edited to a cell-reporting type, and the reverse edit makes a real exposure vanish (also affects the redaction *decision itself*, not just the audit).
- Adds `run_service.historical_check_context(session, results, checks)`, which resolves each result's `(tested_column, expectation_type)` from `check_versions` (#280's immutable per-check snapshot table, already written on every create/update — no schema change) as of the result's own `created_at`, falling back to the live `Check` row when a check predates versioning and has no history — no worse than the prior behavior for that case.
- Threaded through both G1 callers: the REST run-detail route (`backend/app/api/v1/runs.py::get_run`) and the MCP results tool (`backend/app/mcp/server.py::_run_results_payload`).

## Linked issue

Fixes #1489

## Type of change

- [x] fix — bug fix (linked issue above)

## Checklist

- [x] **Manually tested locally**
- [x] **Single functionality**
- [x] **Conventional commit title** (`fix:`)
- [x] **No secrets, credentials, or `.env` files committed**
- [x] **Black + Ruff + mypy pass locally** (full sweep)
- [ ] **Prettier + ESLint pass locally** — N/A, backend only
- [x] **Tests added/updated**
- [ ] **Docs / ADRs updated** — N/A, no ADR change (uses the existing `check_versions` table from #280)
- [ ] **`docs/progress.md` updated**
- [x] **`docs/progress.md` — N/A** for this PR (holding for one combined snapshot update alongside #1485/#1486/#1487 per request)
- [x] **Security implications considered** (auth, input validation, secret handling, PII in logs)

## Schema migration?

- [x] No schema change — resolves from the existing `check_versions` table, no new columns.

## Manual test notes

- New unit tests (`backend/tests/services/test_historical_check_context.py`) against `historical_check_context` directly with a real Postgres test DB: version-in-effect resolution (with the live `Check` row deliberately given a THIRD, different value so a fallback-to-live bug can't accidentally match), no-history fallback, clock-skew fallback (result predates every version), and a result with no `check_id`.
- New end-to-end test in `test_access_events.py`: creates a check via the real `check_service.create_check` reporting a mean, writes a result, edits the check via the real `check_service.update_check` to a max/min type on a different PII-named column, then reads the run through the real API and asserts the OLD result's G1 audit exposure is unaffected by the later edit.
- **Mutation-verified** (`regression-mutation-verifier` agent) against a throwaway worktree with the resolution logic reverted to always use the live `Check` row: the version-in-effect and end-to-end tests fail for the right reason; the fallback-path tests are unaffected either way, as expected since that IS the fallback behavior.
- Full local gate: `ruff`, `black --check`, `mypy backend/app backend/tests` (full sweep) all clean.
- Full backend suite against real Postgres/Redis: **4831 passed, 2 skipped**, no regressions.
- Coverage: `backend/app/api/v1/runs.py` 100%, `backend/app/services/run_service.py` 97%, `backend/app/mcp/server.py` 96% (unrelated pre-existing gaps).

## Security / risk notes

Makes both the redaction decision and the G1 access-audit trail correct with respect to WHEN a result was written, closing a gap where an unrelated check edit could retroactively change what an old result's audit record claims was exposed (in either direction). No behavior change for a check that has never been edited since its results were produced, and no schema change — purely a smarter read of data already being written.

Closed together with **#1479** by one seam (below). Filed this session: [#1476](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1476) (asset endpoints have no ADR-0033 Viewer coverage, excused by four issues closed 2026-08-16), [#1477](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1477) (a zero-row audit sweep logs nothing, so "ran and worked" is indistinguishable from "never registered" for the first 365 days) and [#1482](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1482) (a **scalar** `observed_value` is unmasked on the persisted-results path — a text max/min is a real cell; deferred because closing it needs a decision on numeric aggregates). **#1482 is now CLOSED** — the decision: no numeric carve-out, since a max SALARY is a disclosure the same as a max on a text column; the scalar branch masks under the same known-sensitive authority as the existing list branch, gated on `tested_column` being set (a table-level aggregate with no tested column, e.g. a row count, has nothing to classify and still passes through). `live_probe.redact_probe_observed_value` collapsed to a thin call now that the shared redactor covers the scalar case. |
28	| **Open PRs** | **0** as of 2026-08-19. Both clouds were **deployed to `a0dbede6`** (34 commits, 124 files, **3 migrations** — the whole compliance track), verified per-service rather than from the workflow exit code: api/worker/frontend image SHAs checked separately on each cloud, ECS worker `running 1`, migrate Succeeded, `/docs` serving the SPA shell not Swagger, 6/6 security headers. **G1 (#431) was then production-verified on BOTH clouds** — a member read a run's results and the event was read back through the admin endpoint on a *different connection*, which is the shape the test fixture cannot produce (it reads through the same transaction, which is how four tests once passed against code that committed nothing). The AWS run is the stronger evidence: `exposed: true` with 3 of 6 results flagged, matching the three genuinely failing checks, while the passing row-count and freshness checks (scalar `observed_value`, not cells) were correctly not counted. Config events were verified there too, via a **disabled** schedule created and deleted. **Then the verification found a gap in G1 itself:** the column profiler and check dry-run return live warehouse values and recorded nothing, so an empty `action_class=access` page — which the endpoint presents as evidence — was not evidence at all. Closed by [#1481](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1481), a **destination-based disclosure seam**: redaction follows where the data is going (an author's own preview keeps its values and is audited; an LLM context, file or alert redacts), on the grounds that HIPAA §164.312(b) is an *audit* control that permits access and requires it be logged. No capability was traded away — a masked profile keeps `null_count`, `distinct_count` and the `top_values` counts — and fail-closed suites still mask, because that operator explicitly chose assurance. |

description: Always git checkout main + pull before creating a new fix/feature branch, even mid-chain — never branch off whatever you're currently sitting on
metadata:

---

`git checkout -b <new-branch>` branches off whatever ref is currently checked out — not `main` — unless you explicitly switch first. Skipping that switch silently carries the current branch's commits into the new one.

**Why:** on 2026-08-21, working a chain of fix PRs (#1485 → #1486 → #1489), a docs-only PR (#1487) was opened and the user said "hold #1487, fix #1486 first." The contamination then propagated into the next branch in the chain (#1489) too, surfacing later as a spurious merge conflict against `main` (the classic squash-merge SHA-drift shape, [[dev-stacked-pr-after-squash-merge]], but caused by branch contamination rather than normal drift).

If contamination is later discovered already merged, the fix is: close the now-redundant original PR (don't try to merge it — it'd be a no-op or conflict), and note the process gap in the next progress-snapshot update rather than silently absorbing it.

---
name: project_scalar_redaction_chain_2026-08-21
description: The #1482/#1486/#1489 scalar-observed-value redaction/audit chain, fully closed 2026-08-21 — what shipped and where the seams are
metadata:
  type: project
---

A three-issue chain, each found by `/code-review` on the previous PR, all closed 2026-08-21:

- **#1482** (PR #1485): `run_service.redact_observed_value` never masked a **scalar** `observed_value` — only lists. A max/min-type expectation reports a real cell value, so it passed through unmasked even under fail-closed policy. Fixed with a scalar branch, gated on `tested_column` being set (a table-level aggregate like a row count has none, so it still passes through) — no numeric carve-out, since a max SALARY is a disclosure the same as a max on text. `live_probe.redact_probe_observed_value` collapsed to a thin call.
- **#1486** (PR #1488): the G1 access-audit's `observed_value_exposes_cells` still never counted a scalar as an exposure, even the real cells #1482 now surfaces. Fixed with an explicit allowlist `_CELL_SCALAR_EXPECTATION_TYPES = {"expect_column_max_to_be_between", "expect_column_min_to_be_between"}` — deliberately NOT a `tested_column`-presence proxy, since an aggregate check (e.g. null-count) can also carry a real tested column in its config.
- **#1489** (PR #1490): both the redaction decision and the #1486 audit fix were reading `expectation_type`/`config["column"]` off the CHECK's **current** state, but those are freely PATCH-able via `check_service.update_check` with no re-validation against existing results — editing a check after results exist could retroactively relabel history. Fixed with `run_service.historical_check_context(session, results, checks)`, which resolves each result's context from `check_versions` (#280's immutable snapshot table) as of the result's own `created_at`. No schema change. Falls back to the live `Check` row only when a check predates versioning and has zero version history.

**Verification pattern used throughout:** every fix's regression tests were mutation-checked (revert the fix in a throwaway worktree, confirm the new test fails for the right reason) via the `regression-mutation-verifier` agent — this caught a genuinely vacuous E2E test for #1489 (it edited the check onto a PII-named column, which masks by name regardless of type, so the assertion passed even against unfixed code) and a test-transaction timestamp-tie gotcha (the whole test runs in one Postgres transaction, so every `server_default=func.now()` row ties to the same instant — fixed by stamping `created_at` explicitly).

**Process gotcha from this session:** [[dev-always-branch-from-clean-main]] — a held docs PR's commit rode into #1486's branch and landed on main early via #1488's squash; #1487 was closed as redundant once caught.

Nothing left open in this chain as of 2026-08-21. `MEMORY.md`'s `project_mcp_tier1_expansion` and `project_credential_redirect_1401` entries are the neighboring context for the same `run_service.py`/G1-audit surface.

name: project_scalar_redaction_chain_2026-08-21
description: "The #1482/#1486/#1489 scalar-observed-value redaction/audit chain, fully closed 2026-08-21 — what shipped and where the seams are"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 69e80831-f1df-4b73-9124-56be4ce388ca
  modified: 2026-08-21T20:01:29.885Z
---

A three-issue chain, each found by `/code-review` on the previous PR, all closed 2026-08-21:

- **#1482** (PR #1485): `run_service.redact_observed_value` never masked a **scalar** `observed_value` — only lists. A max/min-type expectation reports a real cell value, so it passed through unmasked even under fail-closed policy. Fixed with a scalar branch, gated on `tested_column` being set (a table-level aggregate like a row count has none, so it still passes through) — no numeric carve-out, since a max SALARY is a disclosure the same as a max on text. `live_probe.redact_probe_observed_value` collapsed to a thin call.
- **#1486** (PR #1488): the G1 access-audit's `observed_value_exposes_cells` still never counted a scalar as an exposure, even the real cells #1482 now surfaces. Fixed with an explicit allowlist `_CELL_SCALAR_EXPECTATION_TYPES = {"expect_column_max_to_be_between", "expect_column_min_to_be_between"}` — deliberately NOT a `tested_column`-presence proxy, since an aggregate check (e.g. null-count) can also carry a real tested column in its config.
- **#1489** (PR #1490): both the redaction decision and the #1486 audit fix were reading `expectation_type`/`config["column"]` off the CHECK's **current** state, but those are freely PATCH-able via `check_service.update_check` with no re-validation against existing results — editing a check after results exist could retroactively relabel history. Fixed with `run_service.historical_check_context(session, results, checks)`, which resolves each result's context from `check_versions` (#280's immutable snapshot table) as of the result's own `created_at`. No schema change. Falls back to the live `Check` row only when a check predates versioning and has zero version history.

**Verification pattern used throughout:** every fix's regression tests were mutation-checked (revert the fix in a throwaway worktree, confirm the new test fails for the right reason) via the `regression-mutation-verifier` agent — this caught a genuinely vacuous E2E test for #1489 (it edited the check onto a PII-named column, which masks by name regardless of type, so the assertion passed even against unfixed code) and a test-transaction timestamp-tie gotcha (the whole test runs in one Postgres transaction, so every `server_default=func.now()` row ties to the same instant — fixed by stamping `created_at` explicitly).

**Process gotcha from this session:** [[dev-always-branch-from-clean-main]] — a held docs PR's commit rode into #1486's branch and landed on main early via #1488's squash; #1487 was closed as redundant once caught.

Nothing left open in this chain as of 2026-08-21. `MEMORY.md`'s `project_mcp_tier1_expansion` and `project_credential_redirect_1401` entries are the neighboring context for the same `run_service.py`/G1-audit surface.

---
name: dev-always-branch-from-clean-main
description: "Always git checkout main + pull before creating a new fix/feature branch, even mid-chain — never branch off whatever you're currently sitting on"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 69e80831-f1df-4b73-9124-56be4ce388ca
  modified: 2026-08-21T20:01:07.657Z
---

`git checkout -b <new-branch>` branches off whatever ref is currently checked out — not `main` — unless you explicitly switch first. Skipping that switch silently carries the current branch's commits into the new one.

**Why:** on 2026-08-21, working a chain of fix PRs (#1485 → #1486 → #1489), a docs-only PR (#1487) was opened and the user said "hold #1487, fix #1486 first." The next `git checkout -b fix/issue-1486-...` was run without first returning to `main` — still sitting on the #1487 docs branch — so #1487's held commit rode along into #1486's branch, and then squash-merged into `main` as part of #1486's PR (#1488), landing prematurely and out of the user's control. The contamination then propagated into the next branch in the chain (#1489) too, surfacing later as a spurious merge conflict against `main` (the classic squash-merge SHA-drift shape, [[dev-stacked-pr-after-squash-merge]], but caused by branch contamination rather than normal drift).

**How to apply:** before every `git checkout -b`, run `git checkout main && git pull --ff-only origin main` first — no exceptions, even "just one more quick branch" mid-chain. If a `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` on a new branch ever shows files you didn't intend to touch (especially a `docs/` file from an unrelated held PR), that's the tell — check `git log --oneline` on the new branch against `main` immediately rather than opening the PR. If contamination is later discovered already merged, the fix is: close the now-redundant original PR (don't try to merge it — it'd be a no-op or conflict), and note the process gap in the next progress-snapshot update rather than silently absorbing it.

Related: a CONFLICTING PR gets ZERO GitHub Actions runs at all (no test-merge commit → no `pull_request` events) — presents as "CI stopped scheduling", not as an error. Fix is the same either way: merge `origin/main` into the branch, resolve, push — CI resumes immediately. See `project_w6_close_state.md`'s "CONFLICTING-PR-kills-CI gotcha" note.

"""`run_service.historical_check_context` — #1489.

Redaction (`tested_column`) and the G1 access-exposure audit (`expectation_type`,
#1486) both need to know what a check WAS measuring when a given result was
written, not what it measures NOW — `expectation_type`/`config` are freely
PATCH-able on a live `Check` with no re-validation against existing results.
Verifies the resolution picks the `check_versions` snapshot in effect at each
result's own `created_at`, and falls back sanely when there is no history.

Skips without TEST_DATABASE_URL.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from typing import Any

from backend.app.db.models import Check, CheckVersion, Connection, Result, Run, Suite, User
from backend.app.services import run_service

_T0 = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)


def _suite_and_check(
    db_session: Any, *, expectation_type: str = "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null"
) -> tuple[Suite, Check]:
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"o-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"sf-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type="snowflake",
        env="dev",
        config={"account": "x"},
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.flush()
    suite = Suite(name="orders", connection_id=conn.id, created_by=owner.id)
    db_session.add(suite)
    db_session.flush()
    check = Check(
        suite_id=suite.id,
        name="values",
        kind="expectation",
        expectation_type=expectation_type,
        config={"column": "LIVE_COLUMN"},
    )
    db_session.add(check)
    db_session.flush()
    return suite, check


def _version(
    db_session: Any,
    check: Check,
    *,
    version_no: int,
    created_at: datetime,
    expectation_type: str,
    column: str,
) -> CheckVersion:
    version = CheckVersion(
        check_id=check.id,
        version_no=version_no,
        name=check.name,
        kind=check.kind,
        expectation_type=expectation_type,
        config={"column": column},
        created_at=created_at,
    )
    db_session.add(version)
    db_session.flush()
    return version


def _result(db_session: Any, check: Check, *, created_at: datetime) -> Result:
    run = Run(suite_id=check.suite_id, status="succeeded", triggered_by="manual")
    db_session.add(run)
    db_session.flush()
    result = Result(run_id=run.id, check_id=check.id, status="fail", created_at=created_at)
    db_session.add(result)
    db_session.flush()
    return result


def test_resolves_the_version_in_effect_when_each_result_was_written(db_session: Any) -> None:
    # #1486's own motivating case: a check that reported a MEAN when a result
    # was written, later edited to MAX/MIN — the old result must not retroactively
    # look like a literal-cell exposure. The live Check row is deliberately a
    # THIRD value neither version used, so a fallback-to-live bug can't hide
    # behind an accidental match.
    _suite, check = _suite_and_check(db_session, expectation_type="expect_table_row_count_to_equal")
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=1,
        created_at=_T0,
        expectation_type="expect_column_values_to_not_be_null",
        column="v1_column",
    )
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=2,
        created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=1),
        expectation_type="expect_column_max_to_be_between",
        column="v2_column",
    )
    before_edit = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0 + timedelta(hours=1))
    after_edit = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=2))

    context = run_service.historical_check_context(
        db_session, [before_edit, after_edit], {check.id: check}
    )

    assert context[before_edit.id] == ("v1_column", "expect_column_values_to_not_be_null")
    assert context[after_edit.id] == ("v2_column", "expect_column_max_to_be_between")


def test_falls_back_to_the_live_check_with_no_version_history(db_session: Any) -> None:
    # A check created before #280 shipped (or seeded directly, bypassing
    # check_service) has no check_versions rows at all — no worse off than
    # before this function existed.
    _suite, check = _suite_and_check(db_session, expectation_type="expect_column_max_to_be_between")
    result = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0)

    context = run_service.historical_check_context(db_session, [result], {check.id: check})

    assert context[result.id] == ("LIVE_COLUMN", "expect_column_max_to_be_between")


def test_falls_back_to_the_earliest_version_when_the_result_predates_it(db_session: Any) -> None:
    # Clock skew / same-instant edge case: every version is AFTER the result's
    # created_at. "Before the first edit" is a closer approximation of history
    # than jumping to whatever the check is today.
    _suite, check = _suite_and_check(db_session)
    _version(
        db_session,
        check,
        version_no=1,
        created_at=_T0 + timedelta(days=1),
        expectation_type="expect_column_min_to_be_between",
        column="earliest_column",
    )
    result = _result(db_session, check, created_at=_T0)

    context = run_service.historical_check_context(db_session, [result], {check.id: check})

    assert context[result.id] == ("earliest_column", "expect_column_min_to_be_between")


def test_a_result_with_no_check_id_resolves_to_none() -> None:
    # Defensive: a result whose check was hard-deleted (nullable FK path, if it
    # ever exists) must not raise.
    result = Result(
        id=uuid.uuid4(),
        run_id=uuid.uuid4(),
        check_id=None,
        status="fail",
        created_at=_T0,
    )
    context = run_service.historical_check_context(None, [result], {})  # type: ignore[arg-type]
    assert context[result.id] == (None, None)

=== #1310 ===
{"body":"Surfaced by a review pass on #1308 (fixes #1275) while tracing git history on the touched files, not itself a defect in that PR — filed as its own follow-up per CONTRIBUTING rule 3a.

## What

PR #516 (2026-07-01, "refactor(frontend): migrate off deprecated antd v6 APIs") already did a codebase-wide sweep renaming every `Drawer width` to `size` (~15 files) plus other deprecated-prop cleanup, specifically to silence antd v6 console deprecation warnings.

#1275/#1308 (2026-08-12) found and fixed three deprecation warnings again — `Modal.maskClosable`, `Select.onDropdownVisibleChange`, and (again) `Drawer.width` — and #1308's own git-history review confirmed the two `Drawer.width` sites it touched (`App.tsx`'s mobile nav drawer, `CheckEdit.tsx`'s trend drawer) were **written after PR #516 landed**, i.e. genuine regressions of an already-fixed pattern, not something #516 missed.

## Why it recurred

Nothing enforces the deprecated-prop migration going forward — it's caught only by manual QA passes (as happened via the #1275 issue, "found during a full real-user QA pass") rather than at commit/CI time. ESLint doesn't flag deprecated antd props by default.

## Suggested direction

- Check whether `eslint-plugin-react` or an antd-specific lint plugin can flag deprecated prop usage (antd ships `@ant-design/codemod-v5`-style tooling for major-version migrations; check if v6 has an equivalent, or if TypeScript's own `@deprecated` JSDoc tags on antd's prop types already surface as editor/IDE warnings that could be promoted to a CI-enforced `tsc`/ESLint error, e.g. via `eslint-plugin-deprecation` or `@typescript-eslint`'s `no-deprecated` rule if available for this ESLint/TS version).
- Alternative if no clean lint rule exists: a periodic grep-based CI check (or a pre-commit hook) for the known-deprecated prop names as a stopgap, documented as "extend this list on future antd major bumps."

Low priority — cosmetic console noise, not a functional defect, and the fix is cheap when caught by QA. But it's the second time this exact category has recurred, so worth a small structural fix before a third occurrence.","labels":["chore"],"milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","state":"OPEN","title":"frontend: no lint guard against reintroducing deprecated antd v6 props"}

=== #1344 ===
{"body":"## Context
CI run [31897220630](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31897220630) — the `Frontend — tests` job failed on PR #1343 (a docs-only change to `docs/progress.md`, so this cannot be a real regression from that diff).

## Failure
```
FAIL tests/components/SuiteForm.test.tsx > SuiteForm — sampling > round-trips a stored sampling block: prefills it, and saves it back

tests/components/SuiteForm.test.tsx:631:19
  expect(screen.getByTestId('sampling-seed')).toHaveValue('7');
                 ^
TestingLibraryElementError: Unable to find an element by: [data-testid="sampling-seed"]
```

The preceding assertion (`sampling-rows` has value '50...') passed; `sampling-seed` was not found in the DOM at that point.

## Why this is filed as flaky, not a regression
The exact same commit tree (main at `7279ad91`, run [31897179103](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/31897179103)) passed cleanly on `main`'s own post-merge CI run minutes earlier. Re-running just the failed job on PR #1343 also passed. One anomalous failure against an otherwise consistently-green suite is the timing-flake shape, not a deterministic bug.

## Not the same as #1254
#1254 (closed) was a different flake in the same file — an unmocked batch-preview debounce firing after test teardown. This one is about a conditionally-rendered sampling-seed field not yet being in the DOM when asserted on, in the "round-trips a stored sampling block" test specifically. Worth a look at whether the seed field's render is gated behind another debounce/async state update that the test doesn't await, mirroring #1254's root cause but in a different field.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Root-cause the timing gap (what state/render the sampling-seed field's appearance depends on, and why the test's `findByTestId`-vs-`getByTestId` choice matters here)
- [ ] Fix (likely: await the same signal `sampling-rows`'s `findByTestId` already waits on, or add an explicit wait for the seed field too)
- [ ] Confirm no similar exposure in sibling assertions in the same test/file","labels":["bug","test"],"milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","state":"OPEN","title":"Flaky SuiteForm.test.tsx: 'round-trips a stored sampling block' — sampling-seed testid not found"}

=== #1411 ===
{"body":"## Found by
Full-codebase QA + security scan, 2026-08-16 (qa-verifier agent, running the local verification battery alongside other concurrent tooling in the same session).

## Finding
The identical command (`pytest backend/tests/`) produced very different results depending on concurrent system load:
- Isolated run: **4430 passed, 1 skipped, 97.25% coverage**, ~92s — clean.
- Run while `pnpm test:coverage` (frontend, CPU-heavy under jsdom) was running concurrently: **1319 failed, 156 errors**, ~649s (6x slower).

Root cause: coverage tracing (`--cov`) is CPU-expensive, and a batch of tests (`test_poll_lock_timeout.py`, `test_schedule_dispatch.py`, `test_session_service.py`, `test_workspace_health.py`, `test_secret_sweep_service.py`, `test_lineage_authz_redaction.py`, etc.) exercise real Postgres row-lock timeouts and cron/dispatch timing against the live `dataq_test` database. Under real CPU pressure, these tests' timeout margins get spuriously tripped.

## Why it matters
Reproduces 0% of the time in isolation and 100% under contention — verified via three separate full-suite runs. Not a code defect in the normal sense, but any local dev workflow running pytest alongside another heavy job will see this, and CI runners can hit analogous contention (shared runners, noisy neighbors), which would show up as a non-deterministic CI flake with no code change to blame.

## Fix (either)
1. Widen the timeout margins on the lock-timeout-sensitive tests (`pytest-timeout` or explicit sleep/retry budgets), or
2. Document in CONTRIBUTING.md that `pytest backend/tests` shouldn't be run concurrently with another CPU-heavy job locally.

Option 1 is more robust since it also protects CI from noisy-neighbor flakes.","labels":["priority/P3","test"],"milestone":"v1.1 Week 7 — stretch (backlog burn-down)","state":"OPEN","title":"pytest --cov flakes under concurrent CPU load (real Postgres lock-timeout tests spuriously trip)"}

=== #1473 ===
{"body":"## What

`.pre-commit-config.yaml` pins hook `rev:`s that mirror the pins in `backend/requirements-tooling.txt`. Nothing keeps them aligned, and they had already silently drifted:

| tool | requirements-tooling.txt | pre-commit rev |
|---|---|---|
| ruff | `0.15.22` (pre-bump) | `v0.15.14` |
| black | `26.5.1` | `26.5.1` ✓ |
| mypy | `2.3.0` | `v2.3.0` ✓ |

## Why it matters

The pre-commit hook is the local pre-flight for the CI merge gate. When the two versions differ, **pre-commit passing is not evidence CI will pass** — a lint rule present in CI's ruff and absent from the hook's ruff produces exactly the failure it exists to prevent, at the slowest possible feedback point.

This surfaced on #1429 (ruff 0.15.22 → 0.16.3): the new `RUF036` rule failed CI on two files a local `pre-commit run` had waved through.

Black and mypy match today only incidentally — the `typecheck-deps-sync` guard forces attention on the mypy block's `additional_dependencies`, but it checks *dependency* pins, not the hook `rev` itself. Nothing would catch black drifting tomorrow.

## Two candidate fixes (not mutually exclusive)

1. **Add the `pre-commit` ecosystem to `.github/dependabot.yml`** so hook revs get their own bump PRs. Doesn't by itself keep the *pairs* aligned — two ecosystems can bump the same tool at different times.
2. **Extend `scripts/check-typecheck-deps.py` (or a sibling) to compare hook `rev`s against `requirements-tooling.txt`**, normalising the leading `v`. This is the one that actually enforces the invariant, and it fits the existing single-source-of-truth pattern.

Fixed in-flight on #1429 for ruff only; the guard is the real fix.

## Related

- Same root shape as the mypy-deps mirror the `typecheck-deps-sync` hook already guards (#54).","labels":["chore"],"milestone":null,"state":"OPEN","title":"Tool versions in .pre-commit-config.yaml drift from requirements-tooling.txt unguarded"}

=== #1484 ===
{"body":"## What happened

On [run 32216451008](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/32216451008) the **Frontend — browser E2E (Playwright)** job ran for **48 minutes** and ended `cancelled`. Every other job in the same run finished in under 6.

The stall is in the `Install Playwright browser` step, inside `playwright install-deps` → `apt-get update`:

```
04:40:44  Get:5 https://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu noble-security InRelease [126 kB]
05:26:20  ##[error]The operation was canceled.
```

45 minutes of silence between those two lines. An Ubuntu mirror stalled mid-fetch.

## Why the existing guard does not help

The step already has a retry:

```bash
for attempt in 1 2 3; do
  if pnpm exec playwright install-deps chromium; then ok=1; break; fi
  echo "playwright install-deps attempt $attempt failed; retrying in 5s…"; sleep 5
done
```

It retries on a **non-zero exit**. A hang never exits, so the loop never reaches its second iteration. **The guard cannot fire for the failure mode it just met** — it is placed against network flakiness and only handles the half that fails fast.

## And nothing bounds the job

`grep -n "timeout-minutes" .github/workflows/ci.yml` returns **nothing**. No job in the workflow declares one, so a hang runs until something external kills it. That is a required status check, so the PR is unmergeable for the whole duration, and a runner slot is held the entire time.

## Suggested fix

Two small changes, both in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

1. **Bound the command, not just the job** — wrap the apt-facing call so a stall becomes a fast failure the existing retry can actually act on:
   ```bash
   if timeout 300 pnpm exec playwright install-deps chromium; then ok=1; break; fi
   ```
   This is the change that makes the retry meaningful. 5 minutes is generous — the successful path takes well under one.

2. **Add `timeout-minutes` to the jobs** as the backstop, so no future hang anywhere can hold a required check open indefinitely. The E2E job is the long pole; something like 25 covers it with headroom against its normal ~6.

## Note

The PR this surfaced on ([#1483](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/1483)) is **docs-only** — two markdown files — so it structurally cannot have caused this. Recorded so the run is not later mistaken for a regression.

Related: [#573](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/573) was an earlier CI flake, closed; this is a different mechanism (a stall rather than a failure).
","labels":["chore"],"milestone":"v1.1 Backlog","state":"OPEN","title":"CI: a hung `playwright install-deps` burns ~48 min and blocks merge — the retry cannot catch it, and no job has a timeout"}

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # ── Backend ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  backend-lint:
    name: Backend — lint & format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install lint tools
        run: pip install -r backend/requirements-tooling.txt

      - name: Black (format check)
        run: black --check backend/

      - name: Launch the API

        run: |

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6.0.10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7

      - name: Install frontend
        working-directory: frontend
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install Playwright browser
        working-directory: frontend
        # Split the browser download from its OS deps (#704). The Chromium binary
        # comes from the Playwright CDN (reliable). The `--with-deps` apt step used
        # to fail intermittently on the runner's pre-configured
        # packages.microsoft.com sources (azure-cli / MS-prod) — which DataQ's E2E
        # doesn't need — so drop those sources before apt runs, then install the OS
        # libs (from the standard Ubuntu archive) with a short retry as insurance.
        run: |
          pnpm exec playwright install chromium
          sudo rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*microsoft* /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*azure* || true
          for attempt in 1 2 3; do
            if pnpm exec playwright install-deps chromium; then ok=1; break; fi
            echo "playwright install-deps attempt $attempt failed; retrying in 5s…"; sleep 5

content.text: That edit doesn't touch untrusted input, so no injection risk. Now adding `timeout-minutes` per job — sizing generously above observed norms per the issue's suggestion.

input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
path = ".github/workflows/ci.yml"
with open(path) as f:
    content = f.read()

# job_name -> timeout minutes
timeouts = {
    "backend-lint": 15,
    "backend-types": 15,
    "backend-sast": 15,
    "backend-audit": 15,
    "backend-test": 30,
    "secrets": 10,
    "frontend-lint": 15,
    "frontend-test": 20,
    "frontend-e2e": 25,
    "frontend-audit": 15,
    "codeql": 30,
}

lines = content.split("\n")
out = []
i = 0
while i < len(lines):
    line = lines[i]
    out.append(line)
    m = re.match(r"^  ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+):$", line)
    if m and m.group(1) in timeouts:
        job = m.group(1)
        # next line should be "    name: ..."
        # find runs-on line within next few lines and insert timeout-minutes right after it
        j = i + 1
        inserted = False
        while j < len(lines) and j < i + 6:
            out.append(lines[j])
            if re.match(r"^    runs-on:", lines[j]):
                out.append(f"    timeout-minutes: {timeouts[job]}")
                inserted = True
                j += 1
                break
            j += 1
        i = j
        continue
    i += 1

with open(path, "w") as f:
    f.write("\n".join(out))
print("done")
EOF
grep -n "timeout-minutes\|^  [a-zA-Z0-9_-]*:$\|runs-on:" .github/workflows/ci.yml

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify .pre-commit-config.yaml mypy hook deps == backend/requirements-typecheck.txt.

Run as a pre-commit local hook (typecheck-deps-sync) to catch drift before push.
Also runnable directly: `python scripts/check-typecheck-deps.py`.

Exit code:
    0 — lists are in sync
    1 — drift detected (with diff printed to stderr)
    2 — could not parse one of the files (config error)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REQS_FILE = REPO_ROOT / "backend" / "requirements-typecheck.txt"
PRECOMMIT_FILE = REPO_ROOT / ".pre-commit-config.yaml"

# Match the mirrors-mypy hook block + its additional_dependencies sub-list.
_MYPY_DEPS_RE = re.compile(
    r"mirrors-mypy.*?additional_dependencies:\s*\n((?:\s*-\s*[^\n]+\n)+)",
    re.DOTALL,
)


def _parse_requirements_txt(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    """Return the pinned packages from a requirements.txt (skip comments + blanks)."""
    out: set[str] = set()
    for raw in path.read_text().splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        out.add(line)
    return out


def _parse_precommit_mypy_deps(path: Path) -> set[str]:
    """Return additional_dependencies entries from the mirrors-mypy hook."""
    match = _MYPY_DEPS_RE.search(path.read_text())
    if not match:
        print(
            f"ERROR: could not find mirrors-mypy additional_dependencies block in {path}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    out: set[str] = set()
    for raw in match.group(1).splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if line.startswith("- "):
            out.add(line[2:].strip())
    return out


def main() -> int:
    reqs = _parse_requirements_txt(REQS_FILE)
    precommit = _parse_precommit_mypy_deps(PRECOMMIT_FILE)

    only_reqs = reqs - precommit
    only_precommit = precommit - reqs

    if not only_reqs and not only_precommit:
        return 0

    print(
        f"ERROR: drift between {REQS_FILE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} "
        f"and {PRECOMMIT_FILE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} mypy hook deps.",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    if only_reqs:
        print(
            f"  Only in requirements-typecheck.txt: {sorted(only_reqs)}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    if only_precommit:
        print(
            f"  Only in .pre-commit-config.yaml mypy hook: {sorted(only_precommit)}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    print(
        "\nFix: update whichever file is missing entries so both list the " "same pinned packages.",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify .pre-commit-config.yaml hook `rev:`s == backend/requirements-tooling.txt pins.

The pre-commit hook is the local pre-flight for the CI merge gate (ruff/black/mypy
all run there too). When a hook's `rev:` drifts from the pin CI actually installs,
"pre-commit passing" stops being evidence "CI will pass" — a lint rule present in
CI's version and absent from the hook's produces exactly the failure this guard
exists to prevent, at the slowest possible feedback point (#1473).

Run as a pre-commit local hook (precommit-tooling-sync) to catch drift before push.
Also runnable directly: `python scripts/check-precommit-tooling-sync.py`.

Exit code:
    0 — pins are in sync
    1 — drift detected (with diff printed to stderr)
    2 — could not parse one of the files (config error)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REQS_FILE = REPO_ROOT / "backend" / "requirements-tooling.txt"
PRECOMMIT_FILE = REPO_ROOT / ".pre-commit-config.yaml"

# Maps a requirements-tooling.txt package name to the pre-commit repo URL whose
# `rev:` must match it. Only tools that exist in BOTH files are guarded here —
# bandit/pre-commit itself have no pre-commit-hook counterpart.
_TRACKED_REPOS = {
    "ruff": "astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit",
    "black": "psf/black",
    "mypy": "pre-commit/mirrors-mypy",
}

_REPO_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(r"-\s*repo:\s*https://github\.com/([^\s]+)\s*\n\s*rev:\s*([^\s#]+)")


def _parse_requirements_pins(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {package: version} for the packages this guard tracks."""
    pins: dict[str, str] = {}
    for raw in path.read_text().splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        match = re.match(r"^([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)(?:\[[^\]]*\])?==([^\s]+)$", line)
        if match and match.group(1).lower() in _TRACKED_REPOS:
            pins[match.group(1).lower()] = match.group(2)
    return pins


def _parse_precommit_revs(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {repo_url: rev} for every repo block in the config."""
    return dict(_REPO_BLOCK_RE.findall(path.read_text()))


def main() -> int:
    reqs = _parse_requirements_pins(REQS_FILE)
    precommit = _parse_precommit_revs(PRECOMMIT_FILE)

    mismatches: list[str] = []
    for package, repo in _TRACKED_REPOS.items():
        req_version = reqs.get(package)
        if req_version is None:
            print(
                f"ERROR: {package} not found (or unpinned) in "
                f"{REQS_FILE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
        rev = precommit.get(repo)
        if rev is None:
            print(
                f"ERROR: repo {repo} not found in {PRECOMMIT_FILE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
        # pre-commit revs for some tools carry a leading 'v' (e.g. v0.16.3); the
        # requirements pin never does — normalise before comparing.
        if rev.lstrip("v") != req_version:
            mismatches.append(f"  {package}: requirements-tooling.txt={req_version} vs .pre-commit-config.yaml rev={rev}")

    if not mismatches:
        return 0

    print(
        f"ERROR: drift between {REQS_FILE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} and "
        f"{PRECOMMIT_FILE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} tool pins.",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    for line in mismatches:
        print(line, file=sys.stderr)
    print(
        "\nFix: bump whichever pin is stale so both files name the same version.",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Verify .pre-commit-config.yaml hook `rev:`s == backend/requirements-tooling.txt pins.

The pre-commit hook is the local pre-flight for the CI merge gate (ruff/black/mypy
all run there too). When a hook's `rev:` drifts from the pin CI actually installs,
"pre-commit passing" stops being evidence "CI will pass" — a lint rule present in
CI's version and absent from the hook's produces exactly the failure this guard
exists to prevent, at the slowest possible feedback point (#1473).

Run as a pre-commit local hook (precommit-tooling-sync) to catch drift before push.
Also runnable directly: `python scripts/check-precommit-tooling-sync.py`.

Exit code:
    0 — pins are in sync
    1 — drift detected (with diff printed to stderr)
    2 — could not parse one of the files (config error)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REQS_FILE = REPO_ROOT / "backend" / "requirements-tooling.txt"
PRECOMMIT_FILE = REPO_ROOT / ".pre-commit-config.yaml"

# Maps a requirements-tooling.txt package name to the pre-commit repo URL whose
# `rev:` must match it. Only tools that exist in BOTH files are guarded here —
# bandit/pre-commit itself have no pre-commit-hook counterpart.
_TRACKED_REPOS = {
    "ruff": "astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit",
    "black": "psf/black",
    "mypy": "pre-commit/mirrors-mypy",
}

_REPO_BLOCK_RE = re.compile(r"-\s*repo:\s*https://github\.com/([^\s]+)\s*\n\s*rev:\s*([^\s#]+)")


def _parse_requirements_pins(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {package: version} for the packages this guard tracks."""
    pins: dict[str, str] = {}
    for raw in path.read_text().splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        match = re.match(r"^([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)(?:\[[^\]]*\])?==([^\s]+)$", line)
        if match and match.group(1).lower() in _TRACKED_REPOS:
            pins[match.group(1).lower()] = match.group(2)
    return pins


def _parse_precommit_revs(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {repo_url: rev} for every repo block in the config."""
    return dict(_REPO_BLOCK_RE.findall(path.read_text()))


def main() -> int:
    reqs = _parse_requirements_pins(REQS_FILE)
    precommit = _parse_precommit_revs(PRECOMMIT_FILE)

    mismatches: list[str] = []
    for package, repo in _TRACKED_REPOS.items():
        req_version = reqs.get(package)
        if req_version is None:
            print(
                f"ERROR: {package} not found (or unpinned) in "
                f"{REQS_FILE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
        rev = precommit.get(repo)
        if rev is None:
            print(
                f"ERROR: repo {repo} not found in {PRECOMMIT_FILE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
            return 2
        # pre-commit revs for some tools carry a leading 'v' (e.g. v0.16.3); the
        # requirements pin never does — normalise before comparing.
        if rev.lstrip("v") != req_version:
            mismatches.append(
                f"  {package}: requirements-tooling.txt={req_version} vs .pre-commit-config.yaml rev={rev}"
            )

    if not mismatches:
        return 0

    print(
        f"ERROR: drift between {REQS_FILE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} and "
        f"{PRECOMMIT_FILE.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} tool pins.",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    for line in mismatches:
        print(line, file=sys.stderr)
    print(
        "\nFix: bump whichever pin is stale so both files name the same version.",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

name="source_connection_id"
              label="Source connection"
              rules={[{ required: true, message: 'Pick the baseline connection' }]}
            >
              <Select
                placeholder="Baseline connection"
                options={datasources.map((c) => ({
                  value: c.id,
                  label: `${c.name} (${c.type}, ${c.env})`,
                }))}
                showSearch
                optionFilterProp="label"
              />
            </Form.Item>
            {sourceSql && (
              <Form.Item name="source_mode" label="Dataset" initialValue="table">
                <Radio.Group
                  options={[
                    { label: 'Table', value: 'table' },
                    { label: 'SQL query', value: 'query' },
                  ]}
                  optionType="button"
                  size="small"
                />
              </Form.Item>
            )}
            {sourceMode === 'query' && sourceSql ? (
              <Form.Item
                name="source_query"
                label="Source query (read-only)"
                rules={[{ required: true, message: 'A SELECT/WITH query' }]}
              >
                <Suspense fallback={<Input.TextArea rows={4} disabled />}>
                  <SqlEditorField />
                </Suspense>
              </Form.Item>
            ) : (
              <SourceDatasetFields sourceType={sourceType} />
            )}
          </Card>
        </Col>
        <Col xs={24} md={12}>
          <Card size="small" title="Target (this suite)" data-testid="comparison-target-pane">
            <Form.Item label="Target connection">
              {/* Locked by design: the suite IS the target under test (ADR 0015 §1). */}
              <Input
                value={suiteConnectionName ?? '(suite connection)'}
                disabled
                data-testid="comparison-target-connection"
                suffix={<Tag style={{ marginRight: 0 }}>locked</Tag>}
              />
            </Form.Item>
            <Form.Item label="Target dataset">
              <Input value={targetSummary} disabled />
            </Form.Item>
            {targetSql && (
              <Form.Item
                name="target_query"
                label="Optional SQL projection (runs on the suite connection)"
              >
                <Suspense fallback={<Input.TextArea rows={4} disabled />}>
                  <SqlEditorField />
                </Suspense>
              </Form.Item>
            )}
          </Card>
        </Col>
      </Row>
      <Typography.Paragraph type="secondary" style={{ marginTop: 16, marginBottom: 8 }}>
        Rows are joined on the key columns; matched rows compare their remaining shared columns.
      </Typography.Paragraph>
      <Row gutter={16}>
        <Col xs={24} md={12}>
          <Form.Item
            name="keys"
            label="Join key columns"
            rules={[{ required: true, message: 'At least one key column' }]}
          >
            <Select
              mode="tags"
              placeholder="e.g. order_id"
              tokenSeparators={[',']}
              open={false}
              suffixIcon={null}
            />
          </Form.Item>
        </Col>
        <Col xs={24} md={12}>
          <Form.Item
            name="max_rows"
            label="Row cap (per side)"
            help="Blank = the server default. Over-cap runs fail fast — never a truncated diff."
          >
            <InputNumber min={1} style={{ width: '100%' }} placeholder="100000" />
          </Form.Item>
